samples.question: The picture shows one dark connected structure: a wide vertical column crossed by four long horizontal crossbars, numbered first, second, third and fourth from the top downwards. Small dark squares are attached to the top edge or the bottom edge of every crossbar, on both sides of the dashed vertical line. The dashed vertical line is the mirror axis. Every crossbar carries the same number of squares, all squares are the same size and colour, and every crossbar is the same length and thickness. A square counts as mirrored only if a square sits at the same distance from the dashed axis on the opposite side of the axis and on the same edge (top or bottom) of the same crossbar. Exactly one crossbar's squares deviate most from this mirror match; on the other crossbars the squares match, or miss matching by only a slight sideways shift. Which crossbar deviates most from mirror symmetry? Answer with one of: first, second, third, fourth.
